what: The Paint Calculator tells you how much paint to buy for a room or a wall. It works out the wall area, takes away doors and windows, multiplies by the number of coats and divides by the coverage printed on the paint can.
It works in meters and liters or in feet and US gallons, adds a little extra for waste and touch-ups, and suggests a mix of can sizes to buy.
uses: Get the liters or gallons for four walls.
Work out paint for one wall.
Get a separate amount for ceiling paint.
Add a price to estimate the cost.
tutorial: Pick "Metric" or "Imperial", and "A whole room" or "One wall".
Enter room length, width and wall height (or wall width and height). Tick "Paint the ceiling too" if needed.
Enter how many doors and windows and the area of each.
Enter coats, coverage from the can, extra % and an optional price.
See wall area, paint for walls, ceiling area and paint, total and estimated cost.
The table suggests can sizes for walls and ceiling.
features: Uses the coverage on your can.
Suggests 10, 5, 2.5 and 1 L cans, or 5 gal, 1 gal and quarts.
Converts your numbers when you switch.

example.title: Worked example
example.text: A 4 × 3.5 m room with 2.5 m walls has 2 × (4 + 3.5) × 2.5 = 37.5 m² of wall. Minus one door (1.9 m²) and one window (1.5 m²) leaves 34.1 m². Two coats at 10 m² per liter plus 10% is 34.1 × 2 ÷ 10 × 1.1 = 7.5 L. The ceiling (14 m²) needs about 3.1 L.

tips: Measure each wall and add them up if the room is not a simple rectangle.
Use the coverage on your exact paint, not a general figure.
Rough, porous or new surfaces need more paint, or a primer first.
Keep a little leftover paint for touch-ups.
problems: Doors and windows are bigger than the wall
The amount looks far too high
Check the units: meters versus feet makes a big difference.
Tick "Paint the ceiling too". It is only available for a whole room.
